Mitigation strategies were defined to address these risks ahead of field implementation. Several coordination activities were completed during BP1 to maintain alignment across project partners. These included recurring engineering reviews with GE Vernova, NextEra, PGE, and BPA; verification of roles and responsibilities; and synchronization of upcoming engineering deliverables in support of potential future commissioning. These coordination steps fulfilled the SOPO requirement for integrated commissioning planning and ensured readiness for any future DOE- supported demonstration. Collectively, the work completed in Task 6 produced a complete commissioning- preparation package, including readiness requirements, interface definitions, preliminary activation routines, and risk-mitigation measures. These deliverables position the project for a technically robust and controlled field activation of GFM capabilities in subsequent phases, even though commissioning itself was not performed during the BP1 period of performance. 7.7 Task 7 - Site Modifications Task 7 focused on identifying, planning, and initiating the physical and configuration changes required to support future activation of grid-forming (GFM) functionality at the Wheatridge hybrid facility. Since no on-site construction or hardware modifications were scheduled for BP1, the work under this task focused on engineering preparation, feasibility assessment, and defining the plant changes needed before enabling GFM operation during a later project phase. A major activity in Task 7 involved evaluating existing plant configurations, electrical layout, communication pathways, and equipment capabilities, to determine the modifications necessary to support GFM inverter operation. The project team conducted preliminary reviews of the point-of-interconnection (POI) metering, POI reference routing, protection settings, and plant-level supervisory control interactions (GFM/GFL transitions, coordinated voltage and frequency reference distribution). These updates are essential to avoid uncoordinated mode transitions, unintended reference conflicts, or protection misalignment.
